In other embodiments, the <figure-callout id="128" label="housing" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">housing</a></figure-callout> <b>128</b>, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b>, and/or other portions of the <figure-callout id="100" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> can be magnetized or otherwise treated to reduce bacterial growth and contamination.</div>
    <div id="p-0044" num="0043" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 1B</figref> is a schematic view of an external body fluid drainage system <b>150</b> (“<figure-callout id="150" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>150</b>”) implanted in the <figure-callout id="101" label="patient" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">patient</a></figure-callout> <b>101</b> in accordance with an embodiment of the present technology. The <figure-callout id="150" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>150</b> includes features generally similar to the <figure-callout id="100" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> described above with reference to <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 1A</figref>. For example, the <figure-callout id="150" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>150</b> can include the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> having the <figure-callout id="108a" label="proximal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">proximal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>a </i>and the <figure-callout id="108b" label="distal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">distal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>b</i>, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> positioned therebetween, the sensors <b>106</b>, and the <figure-callout id="110" label="controller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller</a></figure-callout> <b>110</b> operatively coupled to the sensors <b>106</b> and the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b>. Additionally, like the <figure-callout id="100" label="internal drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">internal drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> described above, the <figure-callout id="150" label="external drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>150</b> can regulate CSF or other excess body fluid flow using sophisticated and individualized methods, and do so while operating as a low power system. However, the <figure-callout id="150" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>150</b> shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 1B</figref> is installed externally, between the <figure-callout id="113" label="ventricle" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png,US09662478-20170530-D00008.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">ventricle</a></figure-callout> <b>113</b> and an <figure-callout id="114" label="external receptacle" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external receptacle</a></figure-callout> <b>114</b>. The <figure-callout id="114" label="external receptacle" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external receptacle</a></figure-callout> <b>114</b> can be placed in fluid communication with the <figure-callout id="118" label="outlet region" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">outlet region</a></figure-callout> <b>118</b> of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> such that it can collect the excess body fluid. As such, the <figure-callout id="114" label="external receptacle" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external receptacle</a></figure-callout> <b>114</b> can be a bag or container made from a range of polymers (e.g., silicone, polyvinyl chloride) and/or other suitable materials for storing body fluids.</div>
    <div id="p-0045" num="0044" class="description-paragraph">In the illustrated embodiment, the <figure-callout id="114" label="external receptacle" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external receptacle</a></figure-callout> <b>114</b> is secured to the midsection of the <figure-callout id="101" label="patient" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">patient</a></figure-callout> <b>101</b> with a <figure-callout id="120" label="belt" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">belt</a></figure-callout> <b>120</b> such that the <figure-callout id="101" label="patient" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">patient</a></figure-callout> <b>101</b> can remain mobile as the <figure-callout id="150" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>150</b> removes the excess body fluid. As shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 1B</figref>, the <figure-callout id="120" label="belt" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">belt</a></figure-callout> <b>120</b> can also carry the <figure-callout id="128" label="housing" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">housing</a></figure-callout> <b>128</b> that contains the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b>, the <figure-callout id="110" label="controller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller</a></figure-callout> <b>110</b>, and/or other devices that operate the <figure-callout id="150" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>150</b>. The externally positioned <figure-callout id="128" label="housing" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">housing</a></figure-callout> <b>128</b> can be made from a durable material (e.g., plastic) that can withstand the rigors of the outside environment and substantially protect the components within. Snaps, thread, hooks, and/or other suitable fasteners can be used to secure the <figure-callout id="114" label="external receptacle" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external receptacle</a></figure-callout> <b>114</b> and/or the <figure-callout id="128" label="housing" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">housing</a></figure-callout> <b>128</b> to the <figure-callout id="120" label="belt" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">belt</a></figure-callout> <b>120</b>. In other embodiments, the <figure-callout id="114" label="external receptacle" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external receptacle</a></figure-callout> <b>114</b> and/or the <figure-callout id="128" label="housing" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">housing</a></figure-callout> <b>128</b> can be secured to other portions of the <figure-callout id="101" label="patient" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">patient</a></figure-callout> <b>101</b> that do not substantially inhibit the patient's mobility.</div>
    <div id="p-0046" num="0045" class="description-paragraph">In further embodiments, such as when the <figure-callout id="100" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> is used for temporary shunting of acute accumulation of the body fluid, the <figure-callout id="114" label="external receptacle" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external receptacle</a></figure-callout> <b>114</b> can be hung on a pole commonly used for IV bags or otherwise affixed to an external structure. Additionally, for temporary drainage, the devices within the <figure-callout id="128" label="housing" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">housing</a></figure-callout> <b>128</b> can also be positioned apart from the <figure-callout id="101" label="patient" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">patient</a></figure-callout> <b>101</b>, such as on a console connected with a power source.</div>
    <div id="p-0047" num="0046" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2A</figref> is a schematic cross-sectional view of the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> for use with the body <figure-callout id="100" label="fluid drainage systems" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout"> <figure-callout id="150" label="fluid drainage systems" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">fluid drainage systems</a></figure-callout> </a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> and <b>150</b> shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 1A and 1B</figref> and configured in accordance with an embodiment of the present technology. As shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2A</figref>, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can include an <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> positioned over a portion of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. The <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can apply varying forces to the <figure-callout id="112" label="external surface" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external surface</a></figure-callout> <b>112</b> of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> to regulate the body fluid flow rate therein. The surface with which the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> contacts the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> can vary in size and shape. For example, the contact surface can be flat, rounded, and/or have a different profile or shape. The contact surface can also vary in length along the axis of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> to spread the force of the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> across the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. For example, controlling drainage of CSF can be accomplished using contact lengths of a few millimeters to a few centimeters.</div>
    <div id="p-0048" num="0047" class="description-paragraph">In the illustrated embodiment, the actuator <b>230</b> contacts one side of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> to compress or “pinch” the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. In other embodiments, the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can apply force from opposing sides of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> or apply force from multiple angles around the circumference of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> to effectuate a similar compression or pinching action. This external compression eliminates the mechanical valve parts within the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>, and thus prevents the actuator <b>230</b> from coming into contact with the body fluid within the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. Accordingly, the body fluid has a clear flow path through the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> that substantially reduces or eliminates stagnant flow regions (e.g., internal mechanical parts) and obstructions (e.g., build-up on the internal mechanical parts) often caused by the complex flow pathways common to conventional shunts. Additionally, in selected embodiments, the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can be configured to fail in the open position (i.e., not restricting flow) such that it does not to impede drainage of the body fluid.</div>
    <div id="p-0049" num="0048" class="description-paragraph">The <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can incrementally or continuously change the flow resistance of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> to regulate drainage rate of the body fluid. For example, rather than a binary open-closed valve, the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can compress the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> varying degrees between the open and closed positions. The <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can thus adjust the level of compression to accommodate a multitude of variables, and precisely regulate flow rate through the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. For example, CSF drainage devices (e.g., the <figure-callout id="100" label="drainage devices" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout"> <figure-callout id="150" label="drainage devices" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage devices</a></figure-callout> </a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> and <b>150</b> shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 1A and 1B</figref>) can vary the compression of the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> in response to the patient's orientation, a siphoning condition, ICP, retrograde flow, peritoneal pressure, and/or other variables that affect the desired flow rate. Thus, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> provides sophisticated control of the body fluid drainage.</div>
    <div id="p-0050" num="0049" class="description-paragraph">Advantageously, despite this precise control, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can also have generally low power requirements because the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> only requires power as it adjusts the position of <figure-callout id="230" label="actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b>. Once at a desired position, the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can maintain its position without power (e.g., “self-braking”). Piezo-electric actuators (e.g., the Squiggle Motor by Newscale Technologies of Victor, N.Y.) include such incremental movement and self-braking features. Advantageously, piezo-<figure-callout id="230" label="electric actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">electric actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can also be small, consume little power when they do move, but can also provide significant force on the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. Piezo-electric actuators can also be compatible with MRIs. In selected embodiments, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can also be configured to permit fluctuation within a desired range (e.g., cardiac effects) and/or transient spikes or troughs (e.g., coughing) in pressure and/or flow rate. This prevents the actuator <b>230</b> from unnecessarily changing positions and unnecessarily consuming power. In other embodiments, the self-braking <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can be combined with a variable resistance component (e.g., a compliant interface member described in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 3F-3H</figref>) such that the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can operate indefinitely without power as long as the pressure and/or flow rate remain within the desired limits. These reduced power features of the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can be of particular advantage for internally implanted valve devices <b>104</b> (e.g., the <figure-callout id="100" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 1A</figref>) because it increases the lifetime of the <figure-callout id="122" label="power source" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">power source</a></figure-callout> <b>122</b> between recharging cycles or surgeries to replace the <figure-callout id="122" label="power source" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">power source</a></figure-callout> <b>122</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0051" num="0050" class="description-paragraph">The <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can also be configured to close to prevent any undesired retrograde flow through the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. For example, the sensors <b>236</b> can detect a pressure gradient directed toward the <figure-callout id="108a" label="proximal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">proximal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>a </i>of the catheter <b>102</b> (e.g., toward the brain) that may be caused by patient orientation (e.g., upside-down), straining of the abdomen, low ICPs, and/or other conditions that may induce retrograde flow. In response to this negative pressure gradient, the controller <b>110</b> (<figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 1A and 1B</figref>) can close the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> to obstruct all flow through the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b>. In other embodiments, flow sensors and/or pressure sensors positioned elsewhere along the <figure-callout id="100" label="drainage systems" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout"> <figure-callout id="150" label="drainage systems" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage systems</a></figure-callout> </a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> and <b>150</b> can sense retrograde flow and trigger the closing of the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b>. Alternatively, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can include a one-way check valve as a purely mechanical method to prevent retrograde flow such that monitoring for retrograde flow with the <figure-callout id="110" label="controller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller</a></figure-callout> <b>110</b> is not required.</div>
    <div id="p-0052" num="0051" class="description-paragraph">The force applied by each of the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> to the <figure-callout id="112" label="exterior surface" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">exterior surface</a></figure-callout> <b>112</b> and/or the effect thereof can be monitored by sensors <b>236</b> (identified individually as a <figure-callout id="236a" label="first pressure sensor" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00007.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">first pressure sensor</a></figure-callout> <b>236</b> <i>a </i>and a <figure-callout id="236b" label="second pressure sensor" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">second pressure sensor</a></figure-callout> <b>236</b> <i>b</i>). As shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2A</figref>, the sensors <b>236</b> can be positioned proximate to an <figure-callout id="238" label="inlet portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">inlet portion</a></figure-callout> <b>238</b> and an <figure-callout id="240" label="outlet portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">outlet portion</a></figure-callout> <b>240</b> of the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> to measure the pressure and/or flow rate within the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> before and after the body fluid exits the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b>. The <figure-callout id="110" label="controller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller</a></figure-callout> <b>110</b> can analyze these pressure or flow rate measurements to determine whether the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> produced a desired pressure or flow rate, and adjust the positions of the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> accordingly. In other embodiments, additional sensors <b>236</b> can be coupled to other portions of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> to measure additional pressures, flow rates, and/or other desired properties of the flow through the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b>/</div>
    <div id="p-0053" num="0052" class="description-paragraph">The <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> and the sensors <b>236</b> can also be used to diagnose flow problems in the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. For example, the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can be closed, and the pressure response can be measured over time and compared to an expected pressure for unobstructed flow, to the expected time required for the pressure to return to a baseline value, and/or to other pressure related values that can interpret fluid flow. Closing the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> during unobstructed flow results in a generally rapid increase in the pressure measurement upstream of the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b>, and opening the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> results in a rapid decrease in the pressure measurement as fluid freely flows through the <figure-callout id="108b" label="distal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">distal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>b </i>of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. Little or no pressure increases observed upon closing the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> indicates an obstruction in the <figure-callout id="108a" label="proximal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">proximal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>a</i>, while a slow decrease in pressure upon opening the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> indicates an obstruction in the <figure-callout id="108b" label="distal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">distal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>b</i>. These flow diagnostics can be performed routinely to sense obstructions at their onset. Additionally, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can be configured to perform these diagnostic tests more frequently when the potential for obstructions is higher (e.g., after surgery).</div>
    <div id="p-0054" num="0053" class="description-paragraph">In other embodiments, diagnostics can be performed during normal operation (i.e., no specialized movement and no forced flow) of the <figure-callout id="100" label="drainage systems" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout"> <figure-callout id="150" label="drainage systems" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage systems</a></figure-callout> </a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> and <b>150</b>. For example, when the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> uses pressure-based control to maintain a constant pressure (e.g., ICP), an <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> consistently operating at a fully-open position can indicate a blocked <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> or an obstructed distal portion of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. Conversely, an <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> consistently operating in a fully-closed position can indicate an obstructed <figure-callout id="108a" label="proximal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">proximal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>a </i>of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0055" num="0054" class="description-paragraph">In other normal operation flow diagnostics, pressure levels within a patient can be tracked (e.g., remotely via the wireless communications link <b>126</b> shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 1A and 1B</figref>) and characterized as “acceptable” or “unacceptable” pressure levels. In the case of a CSF drainage system, for example, an unacceptable level may be one that induces a headache. Using this information, the <figure-callout id="110" label="controller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller</a></figure-callout> <b>110</b> can adjust the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> to maintain acceptable ranges of pressure for the particular patient. Thus, the diagnostic control of the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can provide precise and individualized treatment to ensure not only that the excess body fluid is adequately drained, but also adjust to the particularities of each patient's needs.</div>
    <div id="p-0056" num="0055" class="description-paragraph">In other embodiments, flow rate measurements, rather than or in conjunction with pressure measurements, can also be used to perform diagnostic tests and diagnose blockages. Similar to the pressure sensor driven diagnostics, Rotameters, the “ice cube test,” the tick-tock chamber, and/or other flow rate sensors can measure flow rate during forced or unforced flow and compare it with a desired flow rate to identify partial or complete blockages.</div>
    <div id="p-0057" num="0056" class="description-paragraph">In other embodiments, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can include more than one <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b>. For example, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can include <figure-callout id="230" label="multiple actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">multiple actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> to provide redundancy in the event an <figure-callout id="230" label="actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> fails. Additionally, the inlet and <figure-callout id="238" label="outlet portions" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout"> <figure-callout id="240" label="outlet portions" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">outlet portions</a></figure-callout> </a></figure-callout> <b>238</b> and <b>240</b> can include <figure-callout id="230" label="multiple actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">multiple actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> in order to vary the location of constrictions. This allows the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> to constrict alternate portions of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> when others have debris build up. In further embodiments, selected <figure-callout id="230" label="actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can be designated solely to close the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> to obstruct antegrade flow. <figure-callout id="230" label="Other actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">Other actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can adjust continuously between the open and closed positions to regulate flow rate as described above.</div>
    <div id="p-0058" num="0057" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2B</figref> is a schematic cross-sectional view of a <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> in accordance with another embodiment of the disclosure. However, the <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2B</figref> includes additional actuators <b>230</b> (identified individually as a <figure-callout id="230a" label="first actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">first actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> <i>a</i>, a <figure-callout id="230b" label="second actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">second actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> <i>b</i>, and a <figure-callout id="230c" label="third actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00006.png,US09662478-20170530-D00007.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">third actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> <i>c</i>) positioned over different portions of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. One or more of the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> can provide the incremental force at the <figure-callout id="112" label="exterior surface" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">exterior surface</a></figure-callout> <b>112</b> of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> in order to regulate flow and/or include power-saving self-braking features. Additionally, the position of each actuator <b>230</b> can be adjusted independently by the <figure-callout id="110" label="controller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller</a></figure-callout> <b>110</b> to produce the desired flow rate of the body fluid through the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0059" num="0058" class="description-paragraph">In the embodiment illustrated in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2B</figref>, the <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> further includes a <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> positioned between the proximal and distal portions <b>108</b> <i>a</i>-<i>b </i>of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. The <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> and the proximal and distal portions <b>108</b> <i>a</i>-<i>b </i>can include generally similar materials and can be formed integrally or sealed together with adhesives and/or other fasteners that provide a liquid-tight seal. As shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2B</figref>, the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> can have an <figure-callout id="234" label="exterior surface" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">exterior surface</a></figure-callout> <b>234</b> and a larger cross-sectional dimension than a cross-sectional dimension of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> such that the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> retains a larger volume of the body fluid per cross-section than the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. In the illustrated embodiment, the <figure-callout id="108a" label="proximal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">proximal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>a</i>, the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b>, and the <figure-callout id="108b" label="distal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">distal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>b </i>can form a single lumen through which the body fluid can flow. This singular lumen provides a simple flow path for the body fluid that can reduce or eliminate obstruction-prone areas (e.g., corners, intersections between lumens) that exist in more intricate flow paths.</div>
    <div id="p-0060" num="0059" class="description-paragraph">The <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> allows the <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> to create forced flow or “flushing” through the proximal and distal portions <b>108</b> <i>a</i>-<i>b </i>of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> to clear obstructions within the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> and/or enable diagnostics of flow obstructions. For example, the <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> can compress the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b>, and the <figure-callout id="110" label="controller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller</a></figure-callout> <b>110</b> or remote device can interpret pressure and/or flow rate changes of the forced flow to identify partial or complete blockages. The <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> can also periodically evacuate the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> toward the proximal and/or distal portions <b>108</b> <i>a</i>-<i>b </i>of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> to break up any build up within the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>, and thereby reduce the likelihood of obstructions. The flow diagnostics and flushing can be performed routinely sense and remove obstructions at their onset. The <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> can also perform diagnostic tests more frequently when the potential for obstructions is higher (e.g., after surgery).</div>
    <div id="p-0061" num="0060" class="description-paragraph">In the illustrated embodiment, the <figure-callout id="230c" label="third actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00006.png,US09662478-20170530-D00007.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">third actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> <i>c </i>contacts a large portion of the <figure-callout id="234" label="exterior surface" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">exterior surface</a></figure-callout> <b>234</b> of the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> such that it more rapidly accelerates the volume of body fluid out of the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b>. For example, as shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2B</figref>, the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> has a first length L<sub>1 </sub>and the third actuator contacts the <figure-callout id="234" label="exterior surface" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">exterior surface</a></figure-callout> <b>234</b> of the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> along a second length L<sub>2 </sub>that is substantially equal to the first length L<sub>1</sub>. This increased contact area provides a greater forced flow that can be used to remove obstructions (e.g., protein build up), run diagnostics, or otherwise flush the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> with the body fluid. In selected embodiments, the third actuator <b>232</b> <i>c </i>can linearly apply force to the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> along the second length L<sub>2 </sub>to push the body fluid in a desired direction (e.g., toward the <figure-callout id="108a" label="proximal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">proximal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>a </i>or the <figure-callout id="108b" label="distal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">distal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>b</i>). In other embodiments, the backflushing and/or forward flushing can be performed manually by the patient or caregiver by pressing on the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> and directing the body fluid in the desired direction. The backflushing, forward flushing, and diagnostic operations can be performed either in an <figure-callout id="100" label="implantable drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">implantable drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> or an <figure-callout id="150" label="external drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">external drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>150</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0062" num="0061" class="description-paragraph">The <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2B</figref> can also be used in conjunction with a conventional valve to add flushing and diagnostic operations (e.g., with flow regulation provided fully or partially by the conventional valve). For example, to retrofit the conventional drainage system, the <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> can be placed in fluid communication with a conventional valve device (e.g., a mechanical ball in seat valve device). The <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> can then adjust the <figure-callout id="230" label="actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> to generate forced flow and/or incrementally regulate fluid flow. If only forced flow is desired, the <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> need only include the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> and one or more binary actuators that can accumulate body fluid in the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> and expel it periodically as desired. As such, forced flow diagnostics can be performed periodically on the conventional drainage system to detect obstructions in the flow path of the body fluid. For example, the <figure-callout id="232" label="reservoir" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reservoir</a></figure-callout> <b>232</b> can flush a portion of the conventional system, and the pressure response can be compared with the pressure and/or pressure decay of an unobstructed flow path. When used with a separate valve, the pressure response can be used to test the pressure-flow characteristics of the conventional valve to monitor its degradation over time. Alternatively, the flow rate can be monitored to detect obstructions and/or monitor the degradation of the conventional valve device.</div>
    <div id="p-0063" num="0062" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 3A-3J</figref> are side views of actuators for a body fluid drainage system (e.g., the <figure-callout id="100" label="drainage systems" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout"> <figure-callout id="150" label="drainage systems" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage systems</a></figure-callout> </a></figure-callout> <b>100</b> and <b>150</b> shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 1A and 1B</figref>) in accordance with embodiments of the present technology. Each of the actuators shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 3A-3J</figref> are pinch actuators that are incrementally and/or continuously adjustable between the open and closed positions. Therefore, as described above, the actuators can compress the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> and/or the reservoir <b>232</b> (<figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2B</figref>) to incrementally regulate body fluid flow. <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 3A</figref>, for example, shows a <figure-callout id="360" label="linear actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00004.png,US09662478-20170530-D00005.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">linear actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>360</b> that can move in the directions indicated by the arrows to incrementally compress the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>, and thereby change the resistance within the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. Any of the embodiments described below can be combined, can include interface members that transfer force from the actuator to the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>, and/or can include other types of actuators, interface members, and/or compliant interface members that incrementally compress the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0064" num="0063" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 3B-3E</figref> illustrate embodiments of rotary actuation. For example, <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 3B</figref> illustrates a <figure-callout id="362" label="cam actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00004.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">cam actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>362</b> that compresses the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> by adjusting the amount of its rotation along the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>. <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 3C</figref> shows a <figure-callout id="366" label="lever actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00004.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">lever actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>366</b> that transmits force to an interface member, such as a contact pad or a <figure-callout id="364" label="contact roller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00004.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">contact roller</a></figure-callout> <b>364</b>. As indicated by the arrows, the <figure-callout id="366" label="lever actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00004.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">lever actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>366</b> can rotate about a fulcrum to vary the degree at which the <figure-callout id="364" label="contact roller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00004.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">contact roller</a></figure-callout> <b>364</b> compresses the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>.     <div id="p-0071" num="0070" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 5A-5D</figref> are schematic, cross-sectional top plan views of body fluid flow through the <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> of <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 2B</figref> in accordance with an embodiment of the present technology. <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 5A</figref>, for example, shows the <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> with all <figure-callout id="230" label="actuators" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">actuators</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> in an open position to provide unobstructed antegrade flow through a <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b>.     <div id="p-0072" num="0071" class="description-paragraph">The <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> can also adjust to force antegrade flow and retrograde flow to “flush” the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> with the body fluid. This forces the body fluid through the open <figure-callout id="230a" label="first actuator" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">first actuator</a></figure-callout> <b>230</b> <i>a </i>into the <figure-callout id="108a" label="proximal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">proximal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>a </i>of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>, and thereby clears obstructions and loosens build up of blood, cellular debris, postoperative debris, and/or other debris within in the <figure-callout id="108a" label="proximal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">proximal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>108</b> <i>a </i>and/or the inlet region of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0073" num="0072" class="description-paragraph">Similar to the backflushing shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 5C</figref>, the <figure-callout id="204" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00003.png,US09662478-20170530-D00006.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>204</b> can also adjust to provide a forward flush.
