This forced flow provided to either the proximal or distal portions <b>108</b> <i>a</i>-<i>b </i>of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> can dislodge obstructions (e.g., blood, cellular debris, postoperative debris) in the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b> and disrupt tissue invasion that may occur at the inlet or outlet regions (not shown) of the <figure-callout id="102" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>102</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0074" num="0073" class="description-paragraph">In selected embodiments, the <figure-callout id="104" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>104</b> can perform periodic backflushing and forward flushing to reduce the likelihood of obstructions.     <div id="p-0076" num="0075" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 7A</figref> is a partial schematic view of a body fluid drainage system <b>700</b> (“<figure-callout id="700" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>700</b>”) in accordance with a further embodiment of the present technology, and <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. 7B-7D</figref> show enlarged portions of the <figure-callout id="700" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>700</b> of <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 7A</figref>.     <div id="p-0077" num="0076" class="description-paragraph">As shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 7A</figref>, the <figure-callout id="700" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>700</b> further includes a pressure reference line <b>780</b> (“reference line”) and a <figure-callout id="782" label="controller interface" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller interface</a></figure-callout> <b>782</b>. Both can be coupled to a controller <b>710</b> (<figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 7C</figref>) that has generally similar features as the <figure-callout id="110" label="controller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00001.png,US09662478-20170530-D00002.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller</a></figure-callout> <b>110</b> described above. The <figure-callout id="780" label="reference line" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reference line</a></figure-callout> <b>780</b> can include a fluid-filled tube that extends between a <figure-callout id="787" label="flexible end cap" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">flexible end cap</a></figure-callout> <b>787</b> at a <figure-callout id="781a" label="first end portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">first end portion</a></figure-callout> <b>781</b> <i>a </i>and a <figure-callout id="784" label="pressure sensor" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">pressure sensor</a></figure-callout> <b>784</b> at the <figure-callout id="781b" label="second end portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">second end portion</a></figure-callout> <b>781</b> <i>b</i>. In further embodiments, the <figure-callout id="780" label="reference line" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reference line</a></figure-callout> <b>780</b> can be filled with a fluid that has a density different from the body fluid being drained, and the differing densities can be accounted for in an associated algorithm.</div>
    <div id="p-0078" num="0077" class="description-paragraph">As shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 7B</figref>, the <figure-callout id="787" label="end cap" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">end cap</a></figure-callout> <b>787</b> can include a flexible silicone balloon, bag, and/or other <figure-callout id="789" label="flexible structure" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">flexible structure</a></figure-callout> <b>789</b> and a protective cage or <figure-callout id="791" label="barrier" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">barrier</a></figure-callout> <b>791</b>. The <figure-callout id="791" label="barrier" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">barrier</a></figure-callout> <b>791</b> can prevent accidental compression of the <figure-callout id="789" label="flexible structure" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">flexible structure</a></figure-callout> <b>789</b> and can be vented to allow pressure communication with the environment external to the <figure-callout id="791" label="barrier" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">barrier</a></figure-callout> <b>791</b>. For an implantable device, the <figure-callout id="791" label="barrier" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">barrier</a></figure-callout> <b>791</b> can be designed to prevent body tissue from interacting with the <figure-callout id="789" label="flexible structure" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">flexible structure</a></figure-callout> <b>789</b>. In one embodiment, the <figure-callout id="787" label="end cap" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">end cap</a></figure-callout> <b>787</b> has a diameter of a few millimeters and a length of approximately 1 cm to discretely fit over the patient's ear as shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 7A</figref>.     <div id="p-0079" num="0078" class="description-paragraph">To obtain a desired pressure, the <figure-callout id="787" label="end cap" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">end cap</a></figure-callout> <b>787</b> can be positioned proximate to the desired pressure measurement, and the <figure-callout id="784" label="pressure sensor" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">pressure sensor</a></figure-callout> <b>784</b> can be placed in fluid communication with the catheter <b>702</b> (i.e., the drain line). For example, in the illustrated embodiment, the <figure-callout id="787" label="end cap" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">end cap</a></figure-callout> <b>787</b> is mounted proximate to the Foramen of Monroe to measure ICP, and the <figure-callout id="784" label="pressure sensor" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">pressure sensor</a></figure-callout> <b>784</b> is placed in fluid communication with the <figure-callout id="702" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>702</b>. The difference between the pressure in the <figure-callout id="780" label="reference line" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reference line</a></figure-callout> <b>780</b> and the pressure of the catheter <b>702</b>A can be determined using a differential pressure sensor and/or two independent pressure sensors. This differential pressure measurement incorporates a direct measurement of the pressure head caused by the body fluid in the <figure-callout id="702" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>702</b>. Thus, the differential pressure measurement is equal to the pressure of the <figure-callout id="700" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>700</b> at the end cap <b>787</b> (e.g., ICP). Advantageously, this direct measurement of the pressure head allows the <figure-callout id="780" label="reference line" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">reference line</a></figure-callout> <b>780</b> to automatically compensate for positional changes of the <figure-callout id="784" label="pressure sensor" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">pressure sensor</a></figure-callout> <b>784</b> and the <figure-callout id="704" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>704</b> to which it is coupled. Therefore, the <figure-callout id="700" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>700</b> can derive an accurate pressure measurement regardless of movement of the <figure-callout id="701" label="patient" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">patient</a></figure-callout> <b>701</b> and/or the <figure-callout id="704" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>704</b>. Accordingly, the <figure-callout id="700" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>700</b> measures ICP more accurately than conventional CSF drainage systems that require the <figure-callout id="701" label="patient" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">patient</a></figure-callout> <b>701</b> to remain motionless during drainage procedures.</div>
    <div id="p-0080" num="0079" class="description-paragraph">As shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 7C</figref>, the <figure-callout id="708a" label="proximal portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">proximal portion</a></figure-callout> <b>708</b> <i>a </i>of the <figure-callout id="702" label="catheter" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">catheter</a></figure-callout> <b>702</b> and the <figure-callout id="781b" label="second end portion" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">second end portion</a></figure-callout> <b>781</b> <i>b </i>of the <figure-callout id="780" label="pressure reference line" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">pressure reference line</a></figure-callout> <b>780</b> can extend into a <figure-callout id="783" label="cartridge" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">cartridge</a></figure-callout> <b>783</b>. The <figure-callout id="783" label="cartridge" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">cartridge</a></figure-callout> <b>783</b> can also house the <figure-callout id="784" label="pressure sensor" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">pressure sensor</a></figure-callout> <b>784</b> of the <figure-callout id="780" label="pressure reference line" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">pressure reference line</a></figure-callout> <b>780</b>, a <figure-callout id="784" label="flow rate sensor" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">flow rate sensor</a></figure-callout> <b>784</b>, and/or other pressure and flow rate sensors (not shown) that contact CSF or other body fluids. Additionally, as shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 7C</figref>, the <figure-callout id="783" label="cartridge" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">cartridge</a></figure-callout> <b>783</b> can also include an <figure-callout id="785" label="electrical connection" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">electrical connection</a></figure-callout> <b>785</b> that couples the <figure-callout id="700" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>700</b> to a power source (not shown).</div>
    <div id="p-0081" num="0080" class="description-paragraph">In selected embodiments, the <figure-callout id="783" label="cartridge" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">cartridge</a></figure-callout> <b>783</b> is disposable such that it can be coupled to reusable portions of the <figure-callout id="700" label="drainage system" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00000.png,US09662478-20170530-D00010.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">drainage system</a></figure-callout> <b>700</b> that do not contact the body fluid. For example, as shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. 7C</figref>, the <figure-callout id="783" label="disposable cartridge" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">disposable cartridge</a></figure-callout> <b>783</b> can be coupled with the <figure-callout id="710" label="controller" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">controller</a></figure-callout> <b>710</b> and the <figure-callout id="704" label="valve device" filenames="US09662478-20170530-D00011.png" state="{{state}}"><a title="Show image containing callout" class="style-scope figure-callout">valve device</a></figure-callout> <b>704</b>. metadata.DC.description: Drainage systems for excess body fluids and associated methods are disclosed herein. A body fluid drainage system in accordance with an embodiment of the present technology, for example, can include a catheter that has an exterior surface, a proximal portion, and a distal portion opposite the proximal portion. The body fluid drainage system can further include a valve device, a pressure sensor, and a controller operatively coupled to the valve device and the pressure sensor. The valve device can include an actuator positioned over the exterior surface of the catheter. The actuator is movable between an open position that allows body fluid flow through the catheter, a closed position that at least substantially obstructs the body fluid flow through the catheter, and intermediate positions that partially obstruct the body fluid flow through the catheter. The controller can change the position of the actuator in response to a predetermined condition of the pressure sensor.

metadata.description: Drainage systems for excess body fluids and associated methods are disclosed herein. A body fluid drainage system in accordance with an embodiment of the present technology, for example, can include a catheter that has an exterior surface, a proximal portion, and a distal portion opposite the proximal portion. The body fluid drainage system can further include a valve device, a pressure sensor, and a controller operatively coupled to the valve device and the pressure sensor. The valve device can include an actuator positioned over the exterior surface of the catheter. The actuator is movable between an open position that allows body fluid flow through the catheter, a closed position that at least substantially obstructs the body fluid flow through the catheter, and intermediate positions that partially obstruct the body fluid flow through the catheter. The controller can change the position of the actuator in response to a predetermined condition of the pressure sensor.
